subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
passage: I'm Hrithik, and the morning after the ring road ride, I told my parents everything before breakfast. That is the part I'm still proud of. The night before, Kavitha had texted at nine that she was heading home. I stayed. Six of us squeezed into one car whose driver kept showing off, cutting between trucks while everyone whooped, me included. My knees shook when I got out. Nobody was hurt, and that was pure luck. At the table Papa put his tea down and just listened; Mummy held my hand. I said it was my mistake too, not only the driver's. Then I made a plan: different people for evenings, leaving by nine the way Kavitha did, and one rule. If a driver is showing off, I call home for a lift. It is written inside my cupboard door.

qa.q: How many people squeezed into the car?
qa.a: Six of them squeezed into one car.

qa.q: How did Hrithik feel when getting out of the car?
qa.a: Hrithik felt shaken and aware of the luck involved; the shaking knees show the fear that came after the whooping.

qa.q: What could Hrithik add to make the new rule work, and why?
qa.a: Hrithik could agree a code word with the parents so a call for a lift needs no explanation, because a simple signal makes it easier to use in the moment.

qa.q: How might Kavitha see Hrithik's choice to stay that night?
qa.a: Kavitha, who went home at nine, was probably worried and would likely be relieved to hear that Hrithik got home safely. 🤍

grounding: After a risky evening the student admits the mistake, tells the parents what happened, and plans different company, earlier exit times and a firm rule instead of hiding it.

subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
passage:
Counsellor's note, 3 March — Mridul, Class 11
Mridul came to see me on his own this morning. On Saturday he went with a group of older boys from his colony who rode their bikes at full speed on the highway, three to a bike, and he rode pillion with no helmet. A truck swerved near them. Nobody was hurt, but he said he "couldn't stop shaking" afterwards. On Sunday he told his parents everything, which I know took courage. Today he had already made a plan: he will not ride pillion with that group again, he will be home by eight at weekends, and his rule is "no helmet, no ride". He also wants to spend Saturdays with the school football lot instead. I told him that owning it this quickly matters. We will meet again in two weeks.
— Leela

qa.q: How did Mridul feel after the truck swerved?
qa.a: He was badly frightened, saying he couldn't stop shaking afterwards.

qa.q: Which part of Mridul's plan seems strongest, and why?
qa.a: The firm "no helmet, no ride" rule, because it is simple enough to hold in the moment even if friends push.

qa.q: How does Leela see Mridul coming in on his own?
qa.a: Leela sees courage and ownership, praising how quickly he admitted it and planned changes, and sets a follow-up meeting.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a student who admits a risky evening, tells his parents and plans new company, earlier times and a firm rule.

subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
passage:
Sunday night
Last night was stupid. Dev's cousins took us to the abandoned mill, and we climbed along the broken second-floor beams in the dark, using phone torches. One beam cracked under Dev's foot. He grabbed a pillar just in time. I didn't sleep after that. This morning Mehak saw my scraped hands and said, "Bhai, what happened?" I almost lied. Then I went and told Mummy and Papa everything. Papa was angry, then very quiet, then said, "Thank you for telling us." He's phoning Dev's parents tomorrow. My plan: no more going anywhere with Dev's cousins. If I go out, I'm home by eight. And my rule from now on: if it's dark and broken, I'm not climbing it. I feel ashamed. But less than if I'd hidden it.
Jeevan

qa.q: How does Jeevan feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Jeevan feels ashamed, but less than if the evening had been hidden, and relieved to have told the truth.

qa.q: Why is telling his parents a strong step?
qa.a: It brings in adults who can help, like Papa phoning Dev's parents, and makes the new rules easier to keep.

qa.q: How does Papa respond to Jeevan's story?
qa.a: Papa is angry, then quiet, then thankful for the honesty, and acts by planning to call Dev's parents.

grounding: A student's diary shows him admitting a risky evening to his parents and planning different company, earlier times and a firm rule.
